Responsibilities
The Tech and Product organization builds and maintains reliability of secure U.S. TikTok technology solutions, operations and the U.S. transaction ecosystem, in adherence with security and compliance requirements. This safeguards and maintains the privacy and trust of our U.S. users on every product and platform we deliver.
The TikTok USDS Team is looking for talented engineers to join us in building and scaling core enterprise services and collaborative technologies. As part of the TikTok USDS JV, you will work at the intersection of high-growth product development, robust infrastructure engineering, and stringent security standards, ensuring our platform remains the gold standard for enterprise productivity and platform reliability.
We are seeking a highly skilled Backend Software Engineer to be a key architect and builder of our backend ecosystem. In this role, you will design, implement, and maintain highly scalable, fault-tolerant, and high-performance server-side systems. You will bridge the gap between complex infrastructure requirements and seamless user experiences, ensuring our platform remains stable and efficient under heavy global demand while adhering to security and compliance protocols.
Responsibilities
- Core Service Development: Design, build, and deploy production-grade, highly concurrent services that support our multi-functional collaborative tools and platform ecosystems.
- System Scalability & Reliability: Implement best practices for system reliability, performance tuning, and optimizing application efficiency to handle large-scale enterprise traffic while meeting compliance and security requirements.
- Architectural Design: Lead and participate in technical design reviews, identifying and addressing technical debt, and defining future system architecture to support long-term product growth.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with SRE and Infrastructure teams to develop CI/CD pipelines and integrate services with advanced monitoring and logging tools.
- Operational Excellence: Ensure high availability of services by participating in code reviews and contributing to the continuous improvement of our engineering and compliance standards.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications
- BS/MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
- 3+ years of professional experience as a Software Engineer, with a proven track record of contributing to team-based projects.
- Proficiency in modern programming languages, specifically C/C++, Go, or Python, with a strong grasp of data structures and algorithms.
- Solid understanding of backend development and the lifecycle of a production-grade service.
Preferred Qualifications
- Distributed Systems: Deep knowledge of distributed systems, concurrent programming, and microservices architecture.
- Cloud & Infrastructure: Hands-on experience with container technology (Docker/Kubernetes) and common open-source systems such as MySQL, Redis, or MongoDB.
- Efficiency & Optimization: Experience in performance tuning and identifying bottlenecks in large-scale distributed environments.
- Collaborative Mindset: Strong communication skills and a passion for building secure, high-impact enterprise tools.

TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC is dedicated to the safety and security of millions of Americans who create, discover, and connect with what they love on the apps we operate. The Joint Venture has been established in compliance with the Executive Order signed by President Trump on September 25, 2025. Our foundation is a comprehensive data privacy and cybersecurity program we operate under defined safeguards to protect national security and secure U.S. user data, apps and the algorithm. We safeguard the U.S. content ecosystem, holding decision-making authority for trust and safety policies and moderation. USDS Joint Venture helps ensure Americans can continue to express their creativity, discover new hobbies and interests, and build thriving communities and businesses on a global scale.​
​

Why Join Us
Inspiring creativity is at the core of TikTok's mission. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for our communities, inspire creativity and bring joy - a mission we work towards every day.​
We strive to do great things with great people. We lead with curiosity, humility, and a desire to make impact in a rapidly growing tech company. Every challenge is an opportunity to learn and innovate as one team. We're resilient and embrace challenges as they come. By constantly iterating and fostering an "Always Day 1" mindset, we achieve meaningful breakthroughs for ourselves, our company, and our users. When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us.​

Diversity & Inclusion​
TikTok is committed to creating an inclusive space where employees are valued for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. description_preview:
We hire for attitude over experience!
About Lulius Innovation
Lulius Innovation builds software products for Army Aviation and other parts of the military: readiness, training, and records tools that operators, maintainers, and commanders depend on. Our products run under DoD security requirements, deploy from schoolhouses to operational units, and are growing fast, with new capabilities in active development. We're a small, veteran-owned team, and we're hiring a junior software developer to build alongside us.
If you learned or started to program alongside AI, that is not a mark against you. It's how we work. What we do require is that you understand, and own, every line the agent helps you write. You should be able to read a component and know why it re-renders, follow a request through a function API to the database and back, and spot when generated code is wrong, insecure, or quietly solving the wrong problem.
What you'll do
Build features across the full stack: React and Next.js interfaces, Node.js and Express services, and PostgreSQL data models.
Write the code yourself, using AI coding tools to assist with planning, testing, and refactoring, and review every change before it goes up for code review.
Write and maintain tests, fix bugs, and track problems down across the browser, the API, and the database.
Build, run, and debug our products locally in Docker and Docker Compose, the same way they run in the field.
Work in Git with the team's branching, commit, and pull-request practices, and take part in code reviews in both directions.
Write code that holds up under a DoD security posture: input validation, access control, audit trails, and no secrets in the repo.
Learn the military mission well enough to build what operators, maintainers, and commanders actually need.
The stack
Our products are containerized JavaScript from front to back, PostgreSQL, Tailwind and shadcn/ui, Zustand for state, and Highcharts for visualization, all running in Docker on Linux. You don't need all of it on day one. You need enough of the fundamentals that the rest is learnable, and the curiosity to go learn it.
What you bring
Working knowledge of JavaScript​: promises and async/await, modules, closures, and how the event loop shapes a Node.js server.
Hands-on React: components, props and state, hooks, and how rendering works. Next.js experience is a strong plus.
Node.js fundamentals: building REST APIs, handling requests and errors, and managing configuration across environments.
Basic SQL and relational data: you can write a join, read a schema, and reason about a migration before you run it.
Experience using AI coding assistants to support your own work, and the judgment to verify their output instead of trusting it.
Comfort with Git, the command line, Linux, and containers, or a clear willingness to get comfortable fast.
Something you built, with or without AI, that you can walk us through line by line: a GitHub repo, a deployed app, a class project, or work from an internship or bootcamp.
Eligibility for a Government background check and CAC issuance for access to DoD systems.
Military experience would be phenomenal, but it is not required. If you've served, especially in Army Aviation, you already understand the people we build for: how a unit runs, why readiness data has to be right, and what it costs when software gets in the way. That perspective makes you a better developer here from day one. If you haven't served, that's fine too. We'll teach you the mission, and a fresh set of eyes has its own value. Veterans, transitioning service members, Guard and Reserve members are strongly encouraged to apply.
DoD SkillBridge
Lulius is a DoD SkillBridge partner. If you're a service member in your final 180 days of service, you can apply to spend that time training and working with us through SkillBridge (the Career Skills Program for Soldiers), keeping your military pay and benefits while you build real experience on our products. With positions just outside Fort Rucker and in Reno/Tahoe, plus a remote option, many transitioning service members can do it close to where they already are. Talk to your command and transition office about eligibility, then reach out to us to set it up.
How we'll get to know you
In interviews, expect to walk us through something you built: how it works, where AI assisted, and what you had to fix when it got things wrong. We may ask you to extend it live with your own tools. We're looking for understanding and judgment, not memorized syntax.
Location and details
This is a full-time position based in Reno/Tahoe, Nevada, or in Daleville, Alabama, just outside Fort Rucker and close to the Army Aviation schoolhouses and units we build for. Remote is also an option for the right U.S.-based candidate. You'll work with our engineering team in Reno and Huntsville, with occasional travel to Fort Rucker, Redstone Arsenal, and supported units. Lulius Innovation is a veteran-owned small business headquartered in Reno/Tahoe, Nevada, building for Army Aviation and the broader military.
How to apply (bot check: please read)
To defeat bot and auto-generated applicants, we only review candidates who complete their application on our website. LinkedIn Easy Apply submissions without a matching application on our site will not be considered. Apply here, and include your resume, a link to your work, and a few lines on how you use AI in your work and what it has taught you:
https://www.luli.us/#/entry/junior-software-developer-agentic

Our cybersecurity professionals possess diverse industry knowledge, along with unique technical expertise and specialized skills. The DevSecOps Engineer assesses the delivery and security maturity of each application in the portfolio and builds the secure pipelines, controls and automated evidence that the modernization factory runs on. This role ensures that security is built into how software is delivered — not added afterwards — and that rationalization recommendations reflect each application's true security posture and delivery risk.
Assess each application's delivery toolchain and practices — source control, build and release automation (for example, Jenkins and Bitbucket), artifact management (Artifactory), code quality (SonarQube), Infrastructure-as-Code and configuration management (Terraform, Ansible) and monitoring (Datadog) — and identify manual release processes and gaps.
Assess application security posture as an input to rationalization, including open vulnerabilities, outdated or vulnerable dependencies, software bill of materials (SBOM) availability, secrets handling, authentication patterns and open plans of action and milestones (POA&Ms).
Design, build and maintain secure CI/CD pipelines for the modernization factory with integrated static and dynamic application security testing (SAST/DAST), software composition analysis, container image scanning, Infrastructure-as-Code scanning, secrets detection and quality gates.

Harden container images and environments against applicable security configuration benchmarks (DISA STIGs or CIS Benchmarks).
Integrate governance gates for AI-assisted development, including provenance, human review and traceability of AI-generated code.

About Harmony
Harmony gives every employee an always-on expert for every service request, inside the tools they already use. Deployed inside Slack and Microsoft Teams, its agents draw on a context graph connecting each employee's identity, devices, applications, and history, resolving requests across IT, HR, finance, procurement, and legal automatically, before a ticket ever opens.
With 100+ prebuilt agents that deploy in days, not months, and a 70% no-touch resolution rate, Harmony removes the manual work from enterprise service without removing the humans who should own the hard problems. Built for IT and HR teams that are done waiting for their service platform to catch up with the rest of the business.
About The Role
We're looking for a Support Engineer to be the first line of response for our customers. When something breaks, you're the first person they hear from: you find out why, fix it or drive the fix, and keep them confident in Harmony until it's resolved. How you handle those moments shapes how customers feel about us.
You'll own break/fix and triage end to end, working closely with Engineering and our pre-sales and post-sales teams. You'll be hands-on in the product every day, across integrations, workflows and agents, and you'll help build the support function as we scale.
There's a lot of room to grow here, and you'll have real ownership from day one.
What You'll Do
Own the support queue: triage incoming issues, set priority and severity, and make sure nothing sits unowned
Troubleshoot and resolve break/fix issues across the platform, including integration errors, sync failures, workflow and agent misbehavior, and configuration problems
Investigate root cause using logs, APIs and the product itself, not just the customer's description
Reproduce, document and escalate bugs to Engineering with clear steps, impact and context, then follow them through to resolution
Meet response and resolution SLAs, and keep customers updated in Slack, Teams and email until the issue is closed
Work closely with Engineering and our pre-sales and post-sales teams so everyone has context on customer issues, and route anything that's really an adoption or configuration need to the right owner
Spot patterns across tickets and turn them into fixes, product feedback or knowledge base articles
Write and maintain runbooks, troubleshooting guides and KB articles so the next issue gets solved faster
Help set up the support tooling, processes and reporting we'll rely on as we scale
Required Qualifications
What we're looking for
2+ years in technical support, support engineering, or a similar customer-facing technical role at a SaaS company
Strong troubleshooting skills: you can work through APIs, integrations, logs and system behavior to find the actual cause
Comfortable reading API responses, JSON and error messages, and testing with tools like Postman or curl
Experience with support platforms and observability tools such as Pylon, Zendesk, Intercom, Grafana, or Datadog
Clear written communication. You can explain a technical issue to an engineer and to an IT admin, and both understand you
Calm under pressure and organized. You can work a busy queue, prioritize by impact, and keep track of every open issue
Ownership mindset. You follow issues through to the end instead of passing them along
Experience using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) as a natural part of how you work

Familiarity with ITSM concepts and enterprise IT environments
Scripting experience (Python, JavaScript, or SQL)
Previous experience at an early-stage B2B SaaS company

description_preview:
About Dexmate
Dexmate is building the foundation for physical AI — combining a new generation of robots with a universal Physical AI OS, making robots as easy to build and deploy as software. Today, robotics is fragmented, slow, and closed: most builders are forced to reinvent the same stack again and again, and most ideas never make it past the prototype stage. We exist to change that. Our mission is to democratize robotics by lowering the barrier to entry, delivering a plug-and-play platform for developers, researchers, and enterprises, and cultivating an open ecosystem that accelerates the evolution of physical AI.
If you want to help shape the next layer of human capability — and believe the future of robotics should be built together, not in isolation — we'd love to build it with you.
THE ROLE
We're looking for an Embedded Systems Engineer to own the boundary where our robot's electronics meet its software. You will bring up and debug new PCBs, write the firmware and drivers that make every sensor, camera, actuator, and compute module talk to each other, and make sure data moves reliably across CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, GMSL, I2C, SPI, and Ethernet.
This is a hands-on, cross-layer role. One day you're probing a board with a scope to find why a bus is dropping frames; the next you're writing a Linux driver for a camera serializer or tuning an EtherCAT network for deterministic timing. You'll work closely with electrical, firmware, controls, and robotics software engineers, and you'll often be the person who figures out whether a problem lives in hardware, firmware, or software.
Responsibilities
Bringing up, validating, and debugging new PCBs: reading schematics and layouts, measuring signals, and isolating hardware vs. software faults
Developing firmware for MCUs (bare-metal and RTOS) and drivers for embedded Linux platforms (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson / Orin)
Writing and maintaining device drivers and communication stacks for CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, I2C, SPI, UART, and Ethernet
Integrating camera and sensor pipelines over GMSL (serializer/deserializer configuration, device trees, V4L2 drivers, timing and synchronization)
Bringing up and tuning EtherCAT and CAN networks across actuators, sensors, and power systems for deterministic, real-time performance
Debugging signal-integrity, power, timing, and bus-level issues with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and protocol analyzers
Contributing firmware and software input during schematic and PCB design reviews to make boards easier to bring up, test, and debug
Building diagnostics, test fixtures, and automated hardware-in-the-loop tests for boards and subsystems
Supporting manufacturing, end-of-line testing, and field troubleshooting as robots move from prototype to deployment
Documenting interfaces, bring-up procedures, and debugging playbooks for the wider team
Minimum Qualifications
3+ years of professional experience in embedded systems in robotics, automotive, industrial automation, or complex consumer electronics
Strong C and C++ skills for firmware and driver development; working knowledge of Python for tooling and test automation
Hands-on board bring-up experience, including reading schematics, PCB layouts, datasheets, and timing diagrams
Driver-level experience with several of: CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, I2C, SPI, UART, Ethernet
Experience with MCU firmware (ARM Cortex-M, STM32, TI C2000, or similar) on bare-metal or RTOS platforms
Comfort with embedded debugging and lab tools: JTAG/SWD debuggers, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and protocol analyzers
Systematic debugging skills across the hardware, firmware, and software boundary
Strong communication skills and comfort working directly with electrical, mechanical, controls, and software engineers
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with GMSL or other high-speed camera links (e.g., MAX9295/MAX9296, FPD-Link), MIPI CSI-2, and V4L2
Embedded Linux kernel and device-driver development, device trees, and BSP bring-up (NVIDIA Jetson / Orin a plus)
Experience integrating EtherCAT master or slave stacks (SOEM, IgH, or equivalent)
Familiarity with PCB design tools (Altium, KiCad) and the ability to propose schematic-level fixes
Knowledge of signal integrity, power integrity, and EMC fundamentals
Experience with motor-control, BMS, or power-electronics systems
Experience with ROS 2 or other robotics middleware
Prior experience working in a vertically integrated robotics or hardware startup
Hands-on use of AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Codex to accelerate implementation, debugging, testing, and documentation

America is critically deficient in production of defensive munitions- we currently produce shipborne interceptors in the few hundreds per year while our adversaries are producing offensive threats in the tens of thousands per year. Furientis was started to help solve this problem- introducing a new class of cost-effective, high production rate, interceptor missiles. We're seeking motivated individuals who internalize this problem and are eager to apply their past experience in similar industries (aerospace, defense, automotive/racing, robotics) and out of the box thinking to solve this problem for the US and its allies.
About The Team
The Seeker Team builds the eyes and the targeting logic of our weapon system: a low-cost, mass-producible, multimodal missile seeker that leans on commercial supply chains where they outperform, and vertically integrates wherever possible. On a modern missile, the seeker is 40 to 60% of unit cost and often drives overly long delivery cycles; accordingly, the seeker team is at the tip of the spear for delivering capability to our customers and value to the taxpayer.
Seeker design has exactly two real constraints: physics and mission. Nothing else is a show-stopper, only an obstacle to overcome. We are a small, deeply technical team that drives capability through ingenuity and bias for action and ships hardware that flies. This is a wear-many-hats environment where you must be comfortable "building the airplane in flight" and stepping well outside your comfort zone; a narrowly scoped role with clean handoffs is not what this team offers.
This is an AI-native team. Through fluent use of cutting-edge agentic coding tools, one engineer here consistently out-delivers a much larger conventional team. You will have opinions about where these tools help and where they do not, provide governance input, and build out an AI-centric workflow from day one.
About The Role
You will contribute to the production of perception and estimation algorithms at the core of our seeker: detection, tracking, classification, and aimpoint localization on infrared (IR) imagery and fused sensor measurements, against targets that fight back. As part of the Seeker Team, you will research, implement, optimize, and validate algorithms in these areas, including modern AI and machine learning (ML) methods where they earn their place. Runtime efficiency is a hard constraint: everything you build must run within a strict latency budget on embedded flight-compute hardware. You will work closely with the broader Seeker Team to carry your algorithms from first prototype into flight.
What You'll Do
Design and implement object detection algorithms for mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) imagery, robust to clutter, domain shift, and countermeasures.
Develop multi-object tracking and state estimation: filtering, data association, and line-of-sight estimates for missile guidance.
Implement track lifecycle management: initialization, maintenance, confirmation, and termination under real sensor conditions.
Develop segmentation, classification, and discrimination algorithms that separate targets from decoys, debris, and background.
Develop aimpoint localization and the associated image-processing methods that support terminal accuracy.
Contribute to perception-related sensor fusion, combining IR and X-band radar measurements into a consistent track picture.
Implement, optimize, and validate your algorithms for real-time flight: measured latency, covariance and confidence you can defend, and performance proven in simulation, in hardware-in-the-loop testing, and in flight data.
Research and prototype advanced AI and ML methods within perception and estimation, and help mature the ones that prove out into the flight pipeline.
Skills We're Hiring For
Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Applied Math, Physics, or a related field; Master of Science (M.S.) or Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) preferred.
5 to 7 years of experience in applied computer vision, perception, or estimation on real sensor data.
Fluency in state estimation: the Kalman filter family, including nonlinear variants and interacting multiple model (IMM) approaches, applied with judgment.
Data association at multi-target scale: joint probabilistic data association (JPDA), multiple hypothesis tracking, or modern equivalents, chosen with judgment.
Classical optical image and signal processing as a working toolkit, with emphasis on methods for optical sensors: spatial and temporal filtering, morphology, non-uniformity and fixed-pattern noise handling, and techniques for imagery with a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Statistical rigor as a habit: normalized estimation error squared (NEES) and normalized innovation squared (NIS) consistency testing, covariance validation, and calibrated confidence.
3+ years of experience using python to create, alter, and maintain libraries of algorithms within a modern Git & CI/CD framework.
Bonus Points For
Rust for real-time implementation and familiarity with embedded CUDA
Missile, interceptor, or guided-munition perception or tracking experience.
Track-before-detect or other methods for detection and tracking at low SNR.
IR or other non-visible-band sensor experience, including synthetic-to-real domain adaptation.
TensorRT or comparable edge inference deployment experience.
Multi-sensor registration, boresight exploitation, or radar measurement familiarity.
Modern machine learning fluency (PyTorch or equivalent): training, evaluating, and shrinking perception models with measured accuracy tradeoffs.
Daily use of agentic coding tools (Claude Code or similar) to multiply your output.

Position Overview
We are searching for a software engineer to help us document the diversity of life on Earth. The ideal candidate values meaningful work contributing to a global mission that builds on 350 years of Earth exploration and inventory to identify and describe the world’s biological and geological contents. The person enjoys solving problems, innovating software solutions, learning new technologies, and sharing insight and expertise. Help us document the natural world, and enjoy a collegial and welcoming work environment. You will be a valued colleague on our enthusiastic, competent, and collaborative team.
Biological specimens of plants and animals document the distribution of life on the planet and geological samples document its environment. Our group supports scientists in research centers around the world with software that manages and publishes information about the specimens of preserved plants, animals, rocks, minerals, fossils, and meteorites in their collections. Our open-source Specify platform is used by 135 museum institutions in 25 countries. Specify 7 is a mature, open-source web application built on Python, Django, TypeScript, and React. As a junior developer, you will work with experienced teammates to build features, fix issues, write tests, and improve a complex system used by research institutions worldwide. The platform must accommodate diverse institutional workflows while remaining flexible, maintainable, and reliable. You will gradually take ownership of larger changes as you learn the platform and its users.
The Specify Collections Consortium, (https://www.specifysoftware.org), is a global, non-profit, biological and geological museum organization, legally organized under the University of Kansas Center for Research. The Consortium is headquartered in the Biodiversity Institute on the campus of the University of Kansas in Lawrence, KS. Our development team is intentionally small and operates with a collaborative, relatively flat structure. Rather than emphasizing management hierarchies, we encourage developers to take ownership of their work, contribute across the codebase, and continuously deepen their technical expertise. You will be a full-time university employee with generous benefits including comprehensive health insurance, retirement plan, 22 paid vacation days per year and several paid holidays.
This position is a hybrid position, with days required in-office in Lawrence, Kansas, with a flexible 40-hour workweek.
This position is not eligible for H-1B sponsorship. Candidates must be eligible to work in the US.
Technologies We Use
Front-end: TypeScript, React, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Node.js/npm
Back-end: Python, Django, SQLAlchemy, Celery, REST/OpenAPI
Data and services: MariaDB/MySQL, Redis

Testing and development: Pytest, Jest, automated CI/CD, code review

What You Will Do
This position will be filled at either the Job Title Lower/Higher level, depending on the skills of the selected candidate. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if the candidate is hired at the higher level.
The Accelerator Operations and Technology Division (AOT), Radio Frequency Engineering (RFE) group is seeking an R&D Engineer 2 or 3 for the Low-Level Radio-Frequency (LLRF) team.
The AOT division maintains, operates, and upgrades all accelerator systems used at the Los Alamos Neutron Science Center (LANSCE) complex. These consist of two 750-keV Cockcroft-Walton-based injector systems (H+ and H- systems), a 201.25-MHz drift-tube linear accelerator (LINAC) utilizing high-power diacrode tubes, an 805-MHz coupled cavity LINAC utilizing high-power klystrons as the primary power source, a proton storage ring, and roughly a kilometer of beam transport lines that deliver beam to the five independent research programs. The RFE group is principally responsible for all radio frequency (RF) systems and their associated amplitude and phase control in relation to the accelerating beam.
Due to the different types of equipment that we are involved with, when working in AOT-RFE no day is the same as the next. Members of the LLRF team are involved in the design, construction, testing and installation of high-frequency electronics and software systems dedicated to the control of RF waveforms to achieve optimal acceleration and bunching of the beam. The LLRF team works on ultra stable frequency sources, solid-state and vacuum tube based amplifiers, temperature controlled coaxial lines spanning the length of the accelerator, electronics detecting the beam amplitude at the injector, resonance control systems compensating for cavity changes due to RF heating and fast electronics meant to prevent a cavity arc from damaging amplifiers producing megawatts of power.
R&D Engineer 2 ($106,400 - $176,000)
The Low-Level Radio Frequency (LLRF) team at LANSCE is looking for a candidate with a background in Electrical Engineering or related field to join the RF Engineering group. This is a support role with dynamic responsibilities, guided by the priorities of the High-Power Radio Frequency (HPRF) plant and RF controls required for the LANSCE Modernization Project (LAMP). Duties include troubleshooting programmatic equipment and extending to engineering and supervisory aspects of project execution, such as performing initial calculations, developing specifications, submitting procurement orders, and coordinating testing, delivery and installation.
The successful candidate will be a member of the Low-Level RF Team and will support the development and implementation of digital control systems using digital signal processing techniques. This work includes the development and design of custom analog, digital and RF printed circuit boards (PCBs), as well as writing HDL or test code in LabVIEW or MATLAB for these systems. Close collaboration and coordination with other engineers and technicians on the LLRF team along with cooperation across other accelerator systems groups (such as software, instrumentation and accelerator physics) is expected.

In addition to what was outlined at the lower level, at this level the successful candidate will independently lead the development and execution of low-level RF systems projects as a part of LAMP. This opportunity is currently in the proposal phase and is set to be awarded in early 2027.* ProSync is seeking a passionate Mid-Level TEMPEST Engineer to support the protection of classified and sensitive information through the implementation, assessment, and management of TEMPEST and emissions security (EMSEC) programs. This position plays a critical role in identifying and mitigating compromising emanations risks across mission-critical systems, facilities, and communications environments. The ideal candidate possesses experience supporting TEMPEST assessments, secure facility operations, information assurance initiatives, and government security requirements within Department of Defense and Intelligence Community environments.
ProSync Technology Group, LLC (ProSync) is an award-winning, SDVOSB Defense Contracting company with a strong military heritage and a record of excellence in supporting the Department of Defense and the Intelligence Community. If you have prior military service or government contracting experience, are proud to serve and support our nation, and want to help support ProSync's mission to "Define and Redefine the State of Possible,” please apply today!
Responsibilities
A Mid-Level TEMPEST Engineer will be tasked with the following:
Support TEMPEST and Emissions Security (EMSEC) programs designed to protect classified and sensitive information from unauthorized interception or exploitation.
Conduct TEMPEST assessments, surveys, and inspections of facilities, information systems, communications equipment, and operational environments.
Evaluate systems and infrastructure for compliance with National Security Agency (NSA), Department of Defense, and Intelligence Community TEMPEST requirements.
Identify vulnerabilities related to compromising emanations and recommend mitigation strategies to reduce security risks.
Assist with the design, implementation, and maintenance of EMSEC protection measures for classified systems and facilities.
Support accreditation, certification, and approval processes for TEMPEST-controlled environments.
Coordinate with engineers, security personnel, program managers, and government stakeholders on TEMPEST requirements and compliance activities.
Review system architectures, communications equipment, and facility designs to ensure appropriate TEMPEST controls are integrated throughout the lifecycle.
Assist in developing technical documentation, assessment reports, security recommendations, and compliance records.
Support investigations and analysis involving TEMPEST, electromagnetic interference (EMI), and emissions security concerns.
Maintain awareness of evolving TEMPEST policies, technical standards, and emerging technologies impacting EMSEC requirements.
Participate in security reviews, audits, and inspections while providing recommendations for continuous improvement.
Requirements
Three (3) or more years’ experience in supporting TEMPEST, EMSEC, cybersecurity, secure communications, information assurance, systems engineering, or related technical disciplines.
Knowledge of TEMPEST principles, compromising emanations, and emissions security requirements.
Familiarity with NSA, DoD, and Intelligence Community TEMPEST guidance and security controls.
Experience conducting security assessments, technical evaluations, inspections, or compliance reviews.
Understanding of communications systems, information systems, networking technologies, and secure facility environments.
Ability to analyze technical data and develop practical mitigation recommendations.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Ability to work effectively with technical teams, security personnel, and government stakeholders.
Must hold an active IAT/IAM Level II certification. (i.e. Security+, CySA+, SSCP, GICSP, GSEC, CND, CCNA Security, CASP+/SecurityX, CISA, CISSP, GCED, GCIH, CCNP Security, CCSP, etc.)
A minimum Top Secret/SCI security clearance with Special Access Request (SAR) eligibility or higher is required to be considered for this position.
Educational Requirements
A Bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited college or university (OR) an Associate’s Degree plus 4 years of additional COMSEC experience may be substituted. In lieu of a degree, 6 years of additional COMSEC work experience may be substituted.

Join PROSYNC and enjoy our great benefits!
Compensation
We offer sign on bonuses! We also offer bonuses that are awarded quarterly to our employees and our compensation rates are highly competitive.
Health & Retirement
We offer a comprehensive Health Benefits package and 401K retirement plan so you can take care of yourself and your family, now and in the future. Other health-related benefits include an employee assistance program for those difficult times or when you need to take care of your mental health.

Individual growth is a priority at ProSync. Employees are encouraged to take advantage of our company-sponsored continuing education program so they can get their degree or that next certification they need to propel them to the next level.

A healthy work/life balance is essential for building and executing your work effectively at ProSync, but it’s also necessary to allow you the room to pursue everything else you want to develop in your personal life. Code quality is a top priority. Style guides, code reviews, and best practices are how we move fast without breaking things. You'll also get your hands on a wide range of cutting-edge technology.
Great UI/UX is critical. Aesthetics, usability, and speed are all part of the product. A technically correct experience that feels bad isn't finished.
Collaboration wins projects. Great communication is the single strongest predictor of whether a project goes well.

description_preview:
At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.
We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.
Government and Infrastructure – Technology Consulting - AI & Data – AI Automation Engineer - Senior Consultant
From strategy to execution,
Government and Infrastructure
practice of Ernst & Young provides a full range of consulting and audit services to help our Federal, State, Local and Education clients implement new ideas to help achieve their mission outcomes. We deliver real change and measurable results through our diverse, high-performing teams, quality work at the highest professional standards, operational know-how from across our global organization, and creative and bold ideas that drive innovation. We enable our government clients to achieve their mission of protecting the nation and serving the people; increasing public safety; improving healthcare for our military, veterans, and citizens; delivering essential public services; and helping those in need. EY is ready to help our government build a better working world.
EY delivers unparalleled service in big data, business intelligence, and digital analytics built on a blend of custom-developed methods related to customer analytics, data visualization, and optimization. We leverage best practices and a high degree of business acumen that has been compiled over years of experience to ensure the highest level of execution and satisfaction for our clients. At EY, our methods are not tied to any specific platforms but rather arrived at by analyzing business needs and making sure that the solutions delivered meet all client goals.
The opportunity
You will help our clients navigate the complex world of modern AI, data and analytics. We’ll look to you to provide our clients with a unique business perspective on how data science and analytics can transform and improve their entire organization – starting with key business issues they face. This is a high growth, high visibility area with plenty of opportunities to enhance your skillset and build your career.
The
AI & Automation Senior Engineer
designs, builds and operates the AI and automation capabilities that allow the team to assess a large legacy application portfolio at a speed and scale that manual analysis cannot achieve. This role converts raw source code, database schemas, configuration and technical documentation into structured, evidence-backed portfolio intelligence — component inventories, dependency graphs, capability maps, technical-debt and risk indicators, and consolidation candidates — that directly drive rationalization and modernization decisions.
AI & Automation Engineers work side by side with Application Modernization Engineers, who validate automated findings and feed confirmed patterns back into the pipeline, continuously improving accuracy. The capabilities built here become reusable assets for later modernization, enhancement and operations work across the program.
Your Key Responsibilities
Build and operate automated ingestion pipelines for source code repositories, database scripts and schemas, build and deployment configuration, and technical documentation across heterogeneous technology stacks (.NET, Java, ColdFusion, JavaScript, batch and legacy runtimes).
Develop static-analysis and LLM-assisted extraction to identify application components, technology fingerprints (languages, frameworks, versions and libraries), dependencies, interfaces, data-access patterns and shared database usage.
Build LLM-based capabilities for code and business-logic summarization, business-capability tagging, functional similarity and duplicate detection to surface consolidation candidates, and technical-debt, security and risk indicators.
Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and hybrid (keyword and vector) search over portfolio evidence so analysts and client stakeholders can query the portfolio in natural language with source citations.
Load extracted entities and relationships into graph and relational data stores to support dependency analysis, change-impact analysis, cluster detection and modernization wave sequencing.
Build evaluation harnesses — golden datasets, grounding and faithfulness checks, accuracy measures and regression tests for prompts and agents — and track quality metrics over time.
Design human-in-the-loop review points and capture reviewer decisions, model and prompt versions, and rationale to maintain end-to-end traceability of AI-supported findings.
Instrument pipelines for observability, throughput and token/cost consumption, and optimize for performance and cost at portfolio scale.
Package prompts, agents, tools and pipeline components as reusable, documented assets for subsequent modernization, enhancement and operations work.
